cues: The closed pipe has fundamental v over four L and only odd harmonics.
The open pipe has v over two L and all of them.
So the first overtone of a closed pipe is the third harmonic, but for an open pipe it is the second.
With more harmonics, the open pipe gives a richer note, and for the same length it sounds an octave higher.
